notes: The dataset is reachable and has useful data, but I only pulled the first page. The search UI (search.open.canada.ca/contracts, search_text=illumina) returned 1,692 Illumina Canada ULC contract rows. PHAC dominates the recent rows. The CKAN datastore_search endpoint (resource fac950c0-00d5-4ec1-a4d3-9cbebf98a305) returns HTTP 409 for q= searches through WebFetch. It does answer filters={"vendor_name":"Illumina Canada ULC"}, with fields such as contract_value, original_value and amendment_value. The legacy resource (7f9b18ca...) returned 0 rows for q=Illumina. Descriptions are generic commodity codes (Medical supplies, Miscellaneous chemical products). They never name a platform, so the 6000-to-X step-down can't be seen directly. It would have to be inferred from the size and cadence of each department's orders. Orders are small, mostly $10K-$30K, with occasional larger ones (PHAC $150,880 on 13 May 2026). Element Biosciences shows 3 rows (NRC $337,265 on 30 Jul 2025 and $141,250 on 1 Jun 2026; CFIA $300,000 on 18 Feb 2026), all coded as equipment. MGI Americas sold PHAC an instrument-class item of $1.53M on 30 Oct 2020. Fewer than 10 further MGI rows were not shown. Whether the 2020 item is a sequencer is unconfirmed, and no Complete Genomics, Ultima or ONT rows were seen.
how_to_mine: 1) Download the full CSV https://open.canada.ca/data/dataset/d8f85d91-7dec-4fd1-8055-483b77225d8b/resource/fac950c0-00d5-4ec1-a4d3-9cbebf98a305/download/contracts.csv (large; stream it). Also download the legacy CSV (load-contracts-2020-10-01.csv) for pre-Oct-2020 rows. Filter vendor_name with a case-insensitive match on 'illumina', 'element bio', 'mgi americas', 'complete genomics', 'ultima' and 'oxford nanopore'. 2) Use the Python csv module with python -I, and keep the files in a fresh directory. 3) Aggregate contract_value by owner_org_title and calendar year (2019-2026), and count orders and average order size. 4) Flag rows where amendment_value is not 0 and negative amendments. 5) Check PHAC (the National Microbiology Lab) and NRC for a year-on-year drop in total Illumina spend while order counts hold, which would suggest cheaper X reagents. Compare with the dates of Element's equipment purchases at NRC (Jul 2025) and CFIA (Feb 2026). 6) Pull the procurement_id and comments fields for the large PHAC orders. Alternatively page the search UI, which has 170 pages of 10 rows.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Canadian federal research agencies are buying Element AVITI-class equipment: two NRC purchases and one CFIA purchase from Jul 2025 to Jun 2026.
items.detail: Canada's proactive contract disclosure lists Element Biosciences contracts with NRC ($337,265.31 on 30 Jul 2025 and $141,250 on 1 Jun 2026) and CFIA ($300,000 on 18 Feb 2026). These are all equipment categories, which is consistent with sequencer or accessory purchases. They show government labs adopting a rival short-read platform alongside continued Illumina reagent buying. A second NRC purchase in 11 months suggests repeat adoption, and the descriptions do not confirm the product.
items.source_name: Government of Canada Proactive Disclosure of Contracts over $10K
items.why_new: Named government customers buying Element equipment are not in the known corpus, which lists only core facilities and tenders.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Federal Illumina reagent orders in Canada are frequent and continuing in 2026, including a large order.
items.detail: The 1,692 Illumina Canada ULC rows run through Jun 2026, and PHAC placed about 8 orders between 11 May and 29 Jun 2026. Sizes were $12K-$22K, plus one $150,879.56 order on 13 May 2026. NRC ($27,963 on 9 Jun) and AAFC ($13,495 on 12 May) also bought. This is a small sample of a mostly small-dollar stream, but it shows no abrupt stop in demand from these buyers. Yearly totals and the price trend are not yet computed.
items.source_name: Government of Canada Proactive Disclosure of Contracts over $10K
items.why_new: Dated, buyer-level federal contract values for Illumina were not in the known sources.
